# iliad-094 — renderings chosen for the Iliad (to be copied into conventions.md)

| Greek | `l` | `i` | avoided on purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| ἀγόρευε (Θόας, 15.281, imperfect introducing a speaker) | "was declaring" | "declared to them" | "spoke out" (turned down at 1.384), "addressed" (reserved for προσέφη); follows the table’s ἀγορεύω "declare" for a public pronouncement |
| Θόας Ἀνδραίμονος υἱός (15.281) | "Andraemon’s son" | "son of Andraemon" | follows the table’s Ἀνδραιμονίδης (7.168) |
| ἐπιστάμενος … ἄκοντι (15.282) | "skilled with the javelin" | "skilled with the javelin" | "knowing how to throw", "expert"; ἐπίσταμαι "know how, be skilled" with the dative of the tool |
| ἐν σταδίῃ (15.283, ὑσμίνῃ understood) | "in the standing fight" | "in the fight where men stand their ground" | "in close combat" (kept for αὐτοσταδίῃ), "in set battle", "in the stand-up fight"; follows σταδίη … "in the standing fight" / "in the fight where men stand their ground" (7.241), the same words without ὑσμίνῃ as at 15.283 |
| ἀγορῇ δέ ἑ παῦροι Ἀχαιῶν νίκων (15.283–284) | "in assembly few of the Achaeans beat him" | "in the assembly few of the Achaeans beat him" | "surpassed", "outdid"; νικάω "beat, win against" |
| ἐρίσσειαν περὶ μύθων (15.284, ἐρίζω of skill in speech) | "rivalled one another over words" | "rivalled one another over words" | "contended", "quarrelled" (ἐρίζω of strife is "quarrel", 2.214; "to contend" is turned down there), "vied"; follows the table’s ἐρίζω "rivalled" for contest of skill (2.555, and the Odyssey’s "rival") |
| ἀνώξομεν (15.295, first-person plural of ἀνώγω, hortative) | "let us order" | "Let us order" | "let us bid", "command"; ἀνώγω "order" |
| εὐχόμεθ’ εἶναι (15.296) | "claim to be" | "claim to be" | "pray to be" (the other sense of εὔχομαι), "boast"; Odyssey-style "claim" |
| ἀτάλαντον Ἄρηϊ (Μέγην, 15.302) | "the equal of Ares" | "the equal of Ares" | "like Ares", "peer of Ares"; follows ἀτάλαντον "the equal of" in the table (2.169) |
| ὑσμίνην ἤρτυνον (15.303) | "set the battle in order" | "set the battle in order" | "arrayed", "marshalled", "prepared"; ἀρτύνω "set in order" |
| προὔτυψαν ἀολλέες (15.306) | "pressed forward in a close mass" | "pressed forward in a close mass" | "charged", "surged" (each adds force); ἀολλέες keeps the table’s "in a close mass" |
| μακρὰ βιβάς (15.307) | "striding with long strides" | "striding with long strides" | "taking giant strides", "with great strides"; keeps the table’s προβιβάς "striding forward" |
| εἱμένος ὤμοιιν νεφέλην (15.308) | "clothed on his two shoulders in cloud" | "wrapped in cloud about the shoulders" | "veiled in mist" (kept for ἠέρι); follows the table’s νεφέλῃ εἰλυμένος ὤμους "wrapped about the shoulders in cloud" (5.186) |
| αἰγίδα θοῦριν δεινὴν ἀμφιδάσειαν ἀριπρεπέ’ (15.308–309) | "the aegis, impetuous, dread, shaggy-all-round, outstanding" | "the impetuous aegis, dread, shaggy all round, outstanding" | "tasselled", "fringed" (decides the sense of the rare ἀμφιδάσεια, from δασύς "shaggy"; the note says "perhaps for the tassels"), "furious", "terrible", "conspicuous"; θοῦρις "impetuous" (4.234), δεινός "dread", ἀριπρεπής "outstanding" (8.390) |
| ἐς φόβον ἀνδρῶν (15.310) | "for the flight of men" | "to put men to flight" | "for the terror of men" (φόβος in battle is "flight", 5.252) |
| ἧκε φόβον (15.326) | "sent flight" | "sent flight among them" | "sent panic" (reserved for φύζα), "terror"; follows the table’s φόβος "flight" |
| ὑπέμειναν ἀολλέες (15.312) | "stood their ground in a close mass" | "stood firm in a close mass" | "awaited", "withstood"; ὑπομένω "stand firm, hold one’s ground" |
| ὦρτο δ’ ἀϋτή ὀξεῖ’ ἀμφοτέρωθεν (15.312–313) | "arose a battle-cry shrill from both sides" | "a shrill battle-cry arose from both sides" | "clamour", "shout"; follows the table’s ἀϋτή "battle-cry" (1.492) |
| ἀπὸ νευρῆφι … ὀϊστοί θρῷσκον (15.313–314) | "from the bowstring the arrows leapt" | "the arrows leapt from the bowstrings" | "flew", "sprang"; θρῴσκω "leap", ὀϊστός "arrow" |
| ἔχ’ ἀτρέμα (αἰγίδα, 15.318) | "held … motionless" | "held … motionless" | "steady", "quietly"; follows the table’s ἀτρέμας "motionless" (5.523) |
| κατ’ ἐνῶπα ἰδών (15.320) | "looking face to face" | "looked … full in the face" | "straight at", "to their faces"; ἐνῶπα "face to face" |
| Δαναῶν ταχυπώλων (15.320) | "the swift-colted Danaans" | "the Danaans with their swift colts" | "swift-horsed", "with swift horses"; the table’s ταχύπωλος row (4.232, 5.316), unchanged |
| θυμὸν ἐν στήθεσσιν ἔθελξε (15.321–322) | "their heart in their breasts he enchanted" | "he enchanted the heart in their breasts" | "bewitched", "charmed away", "stunned"; θέλγω "enchant" (10.291) and θυμός "heart" |
| θούριδος ἀλκῆς (15.322) | "impetuous might" | "their impetuous might" | the table’s row (4.234), unchanged |
| βοῶν ἀγέλην ἢ πῶϋ μέγ’ οἰῶν (15.323) | "a herd of cattle or a great flock of sheep" | "a herd of cattle or a great flock of sheep" | "drove", "mob"; ἀγέλη "herd", πῶυ "flock" |
| κλονέωσι (15.324) | "throw into confusion" | "throw … into confusion" | "scatter" (kept for κεδάννυμι), "stampede"; the table’s κλονέω |
| νυκτὸς ἀμολγῷ (μελαίνης, 15.324) | "in the dead of black night" | "in the depths of black night" (+ note: the sense of ἀμολγός is not known) | "milking-time", "darkness" (each decides an open question); follows the table’s ἐν νυκτὸς ἀμολγῷ (11.173) with μελαίνης added |
| σημάντορος οὐ παρεόντος (15.325, of a herd) | "no order-giver being present" | "with no herdsman there" | "shepherd", "marker"; σημάντωρ is "one who gives orders" in the table (4.431), and "herdsman" is the sense that the herd and flock require; the note says so |
| ἐφόβηθεν Ἀχαιοὶ ἀνάλκιδες (15.326) | "were put to flight the Achaeans, without might" | "the Achaeans were put to flight, without might" | "fled in terror"; ἀνάλκις "without might" |
| κῦδος ὄπαζεν (15.326, imperfect) | "was granting glory" | "granted glory" | "gave", "bestowed"; follows the table’s κῦδος ὄπαζε "grant … glory" |
| ἔνθα δ’ ἀνὴρ ἕλεν ἄνδρα (15.328) | "a man took a man" | "a man killed a man" | "slew", "caught", "man killed man" (compressed, and it sounds like a formula of another language); follows the table’s ἕλε "took" in `l`, "killed" in `i` (5.37), with the article added in `i` as `l` has it |
| ἔπεφνε (Ἕκτωρ μὲν Στιχίον τε καὶ Ἀρκεσίλαον ἔπεφνε, 15.329) | "killed" | "killed" | "slew" (the table’s ἔπεφνε is "killed" in both layers, 4.397, following odyssey-055), "destroyed"; the aorist of φένω |
| χαλκοχιτώνων (Βοιωτῶν, 15.330) | "bronze-shirted" | "bronze-shirted" | the table’s χαλκοχιτών (3.127) |
| πιστὸν ἑταῖρον (15.331) | "trusty companion" | "trusty companion" | "faithful", "loyal", "friend"; πιστός "trusty", ἑταῖρος "companion" |
| ἀρχὸς … Ἀθηναίων (15.337) | "a commander of the Athenians" | "a commander of the Athenians" | the table’s ἀρχοὶ Ἀθηναίων (13.196) |
| ἐτέτυκτο (15.337, pluperfect passive of τεύχω) | "was" | "was" | "had been made", "had become"; the note gives the literal sense |
| καλέσκετο (15.338, iterative) | "he was called" | "was called" | "used to be called" (the iteration is not carried into English) |
| Μηκιστεύς · Ἐχίος · Πολίτης · Κλονίος · Ἀγήνωρ · Δηΐοχος · Ἴασος · Σφῆλος · Βουκόλος · Ἀρκεσίλαος (15.329–342) | "Mecisteus" · "Echius" · "Polites" · "Clonius" · "Agenor" · "Deiochus" · "Iasus" · "Sphelus" · "Bucolus" · "Arcesilaus" | same | "Mekisteus", "Boukolos"; Latin spellings as in the table’s names (Stichius, Meges, Medon, Podarces) |
| Δηΐοχον … βάλε νείατον ὦμον (15.341) | "the lowest part of the shoulder" | "in the lowest part of the shoulder" | "the base of the shoulder", "the bottom of the shoulder"; follows the table’s νείατος "lowest part" (5.293, 5.857), the accusative naming the part struck |
| ἐνάριζον ἀπ’ ἔντεα (15.343) | "were despoiling … of their gear" | "were stripping … of their gear" | "slew", "killed" (kept for ἔπεφνε), "armour" (the table’s `i` for ἐναρίζω is "stripped them of their armour", 5.155, but here ἔντεα are named and keep "gear", 3.339); follows the table’s ἐναρίζω `l` "despoil" (5.155, 5.151, 4.488) and `i` "strip" |
| ἐνιπλήξαντες (15.344) | "having dashed into" | "dashed into" | "crashing", "tumbling"; follows the table’s τάφρῳ ἐνιπλήξωμεν ὀρυκτῇ (12.72) |
| δύοντο δὲ τεῖχος ἀνάγκῃ (15.345) | "went into the wall by necessity" | "went into the wall of necessity" | "sheltered behind the wall", "were driven"; δύω "go into" with the accusative |
| ὃν δ’ ἂν ἐγὼν ἀπάνευθε νεῶν ἑτέρωθι νοήσω (15.348) | "whomever I shall perceive apart from the ships, elsewhere" | "whomever I see apart from the ships, off elsewhere" | "far from the ships", "on the other side"; follows the table’s ἀπάνευθε "apart" and νοήσω "I shall perceive" (8.10) |
| θάνατον μητίσομαι (15.349) | "I will devise death" | "I will devise death for him" | "plot", "contrive"; μητίομαι "devise" |
| πυρὸς λελάχωσι θανόντα (15.350) | "will give a share of fire … when dead" | "will not give him, dead, his share of fire" | "burn", "grant the rites"; follows the table’s πυρός … λελάχωσι "give a share of fire" (7.79) |
| γνωτοί τε γνωταί τε (15.350) | "kinsmen and kinswomen" | "kinsmen and kinswomen" | "brothers and sisters", "relatives"; γνωτός "kinsman" (13.696), the feminine added |
| κύνες ἐρύουσι (15.351) | "dogs will drag" | "dogs will drag him" | "tear", "devour"; ἐρύω "drag" |
| μάστιγι κατωμαδόν (15.352) | "with the whip from the shoulder" | "with the whip, laid on from the shoulder" | "over the shoulder", "with a flourish"; κατωμαδόν "from the shoulder" (the note says it is rare) |
| ὁμοκλήσαντες (15.354, no object) | "having shouted" | "shouted" | "cheering", "rebuking"; the table’s ὁμοκλάω is "shout at" (5.439, 6.54), and the "at" is dropped because the verb has no object here |
| ἐρυσάρματας ἵππους (15.354) | "chariot-drawing horses" | "chariot-drawing horses" | "chariot-pulling", "car-drawing"; ἐρύω "draw", ἅρμα "chariot" |
| ἠχῇ θεσπεσίῃ (15.355) | "with a wondrous din" | "with a wondrous din" | "divine", "godlike" (reserved for δῖος, θεῖος); follows the table’s θεσπεσίη "wondrous" (9.2) |
| ὄχθας καπέτοιο βαθείης ποσσὶν ἐρείπων … κατέβαλλε (15.356–357) | "the banks of the deep ditch with his feet bringing down … threw them into the middle" | "brought down the banks of the deep ditch with his feet and threw them into the middle" | "trench" (the table’s τάφρος and κάπετος are "ditch", 7.341, 9.67), "kicking over"; ἐρείπω here transitive, "bring down" |
| γεφύρωσεν δὲ κέλευθον μακρὴν ἠδ’ εὐρεῖαν (15.357–358) | "bridged a way long and wide" | "bridged a way, long and wide" | "road", "causeway", "path"; γεφυρόω "bridge", κέλευθος "way" (sing.) |
| ὅσον τ’ ἐπὶ δουρὸς ἐρωή γίγνεται (15.358–359) | "as great as the rush of a spear is" | "as far as the rush of a spear goes" | "a spear’s throw", "a spear’s cast" (each pins the measure); ἐρωή "rush" (4.542) |
| φαλαγγηδόν (15.360) | "in phalanx-fashion" | "in a phalanx" | "in battalions", "in close ranks"; the adverb in -δόν |
| αἰγίδ’ ἔχων ἐρίτιμον (15.361) | "holding the much-honoured aegis" | "holding the much honoured aegis" | "precious aegis"; follows the table’s ἐρίτιμον "much-honoured" (2.447) |
| ἔρειπε δὲ τεῖχος Ἀχαιῶν ῥεῖα μάλ’ (15.361–362) | "he was bringing down the wall of the Achaeans very easily" | "he brought down the wall of the Achaeans very easily" | "razed", "levelled", "tore down"; ἐρείπω "bring down" |
| ἀθύρματα (15.363, a child’s sandwork) | "playthings" | "playthings" | **departs from the Odyssey table’s `i` "trinkets" (ἀθύρματα, 15.416)**: "trinkets" suits wares, not what a child builds on a shore; "toys" is avoided as too modern; `l` keeps "playthings" as in the Odyssey |
| ψάμαθον … ἂψ αὖτις συνέχευε (15.362–364) | "sand … jumbles together" | "tumbles them back into a jumble" | "scatters" (kept for κεδάννυμι), "kicks over", "sweeps away"; συγχέω "jumble together"; ψάμαθος "sand" (2.800) |
| ἤϊε Φοῖβε (15.365) | "Ēïe Phoebus" (ἤϊε untranslated) | "Phoebus" (ἤϊε dropped; the note says so) | "healer", "Paean", "far-shooter" (each decides the unknown meaning of ἤϊε) |
| κάματον … ὀϊζύν (15.365) | "toil … distress" | "toil and distress" | "labour and trouble", "pain"; ὀϊζύς "distress" (15.342), κάματος "toil" |
| σύγχεας (15.366) | "confounded" | "undid" | "threw into confusion" (kept for the table’s σύγχει θυμόν, 13.808); συγχέω "jumble together", the verb of the child in the line before |
| ἐνῶρσας φύζαν (15.366) | "panic you roused" | "stirred up panic" | "flight" (φόβος); φύζα "panic" (9.2) |
| ὣς οἳ μὲν παρὰ νηυσὶν ἐρητύοντο μένοντες (15.367–369) | "So these by the ships were held back, remaining" | "So these held where they were beside the ships, standing fast" | the English of iliad-049 (15.368–369 there with οἳ μὲν δὴ), with only the opening particles changed; "Then" and "Thus" avoided |
| Γερήνιος οὖρος Ἀχαιῶν (Νέστωρ, 15.370) | "the Gerenian, warden of the Achaeans" | "the Gerenian, warden of the Achaeans" | the table’s row (8.80–81, 3.411), unchanged |
| εὔχετο χεῖρ’ ὀρέγων εἰς οὐρανὸν ἀστερόεντα (15.371, second half of a line also in the Odyssey) | "prayed, stretching out his hands to the starry sky:" | "prayed, stretching out his hands to the starry sky:" | the Odyssey’s English (odyssey-044), unchanged |
| Ζεῦ πάτερ (15.372) | "Father Zeus" | "Father Zeus" | as shipped in the Odyssey; no other form of address is used |
| ἐν Ἄργεΐ περ πολυπύρῳ (15.372) | "in Argos, rich in wheat" | "in Argos, rich in wheat" | "wheat-rich" (turned down in the Odyssey table’s πολύπυρος "rich in wheat", 14.335), "fertile", "rich in grain" (grain is not specific to wheat); πολύπυρος "with much wheat" (πυρός, not πῦρ "fire"); `i` keeps the epithet as a trailing phrase |
| ὑπέσχεο καὶ κατένευσας (15.374) | "you promised and nodded assent" | "you gave your promise and nodded your assent" | "undertook" (kept for ὑπέστην); follows the table’s ὑπέσχετο "promised" and κατένευσα "nodded assent" |
| τῶν μνῆσαι (15.375) | "of those things remember" | "remember them" | "recall", "bear in mind"; μιμνῄσκομαι + genitive |
| νηλεὲς ἦμαρ (15.375) | "the pitiless day" | "the pitiless day" | "cruel", "ruthless", "merciless"; follows the table’s ἀμύνετε νηλεὲς ἦμαρ "ward off the pitiless day" (11.588) and νηλεής "pitiless" (8.507, 8.525) |
| Ὀλύμπιε (15.375) | "Olympian" | "Olympian" | "lord of Olympus"; the vocative of Ὀλύμπιος |
| μηδ’ οὕτω Τρώεσσιν ἔα δάμνασθαι Ἀχαιούς (15.376) | "and not thus by the Trojans allow to be subdued the Achaeans.”" | "and do not let the Achaeans be subdued by the Trojans like this.”" | the English of iliad-048 (which has the line after "At least allow us ourselves to flee away and escape"), kept with "and" added because this line follows a different line |

One departure from an Odyssey rendering is made in this part: ἀθύρματα `i` "playthings" for the Odyssey’s "trinkets" (see the row, with the reason). Whole-unit repeats (15.285, 15.294, 15.333–334a, 15.334b–336) take the published `l` and `i` unchanged; 15.300 takes the published words, since the Greek differs only in its final stop.
